narrative_synthesis: Seller finance is still the meta, and today's winner was a short personal win with real numbers and a clear call to action. Drafts for today: (1) a short 'ask the seller' post with one concrete number, (2) the contrarian 'terms make a good deal better, not a bad deal good' take, (3) a Philly rent-vs-expenses reality check that invites replies.

drafts.draft_en:
The best deal I ever heard about started with one question:

"Would you be open to financing the sale?"

Tired landlords say yes more than you think. No bank, no 25% down, terms you both agree on.

If you're talking to sellers in Philly, ask it every time.
drafts.pattern: short personal-style win + all-caps-energy call to action (ask the seller)
drafts.video_tip: Selfie video walking past a Philly rowhouse block. Say the one question to camera in the first 3 seconds, then why it works. Under 30s.

drafts.draft_en:
Seller financing should make a good deal better.

It should never be the reason you do a bad one.

Run the numbers like it's a bank loan first. If it only works because of the terms, walk.
drafts.pattern: contrarian 'should never be the reason' framing
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, two lines on screen as you say them. 15-20s. End on 'walk.'

drafts.draft_en:
Philly rental brings in $1,800 a month.

Now take out the mortgage, taxes, insurance, repairs, vacancy and the water bill.

What's actually left on yours? Be honest.
drafts.video_tip: Skip video, or a quick whiteboard subtraction from $1,800 down. Reply to every answer in the first hour. Swap in your real numbers before posting.
